text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a short sync on GQA/MQA invocation boundaries. From perf experiments it's not obvious whether we should group by "request window" (arrival-time buckets) or by "model-seq-len bins". Can we chat?
jordan: I think we landed on hybrid in the doc but didn't finalize the fallback semantics. Hybrid = time-window primary, fallback to seq-len grouping when mismatch causes kernel thrash.
nina: What do you mean by "kernel thrash"? Example?
maria: When a group mixes 128 and 2048 queries the attention kernel picks a heavy path and the small queries pay the penalty (memory copies + worse kernel). Latency p95 spikes.
ishaan: Running numbers from last perf run: grouped by 50ms window => throughput 1.9x, p95 latency 420ms; seq-len binning => throughput 1.5x, p95 220ms. So time-window better for throughput but worse for tail.
lee: That makes sense. We also saw KV cache reuse is higher with time-window grouping which helps cost. But that assumes queries share prefixes frequently.
maria: Right. Proposal: Keep time-window grouping as default (lowest avg cost) but add an "invocation boundary" contract on the SDK: callers can opt into "strict homogeneity" hint per request (e.g., prefer seq-len binning) and a per-request TTL so we don't block for long.
jordan: Suggest API change: add "grouping_hint": "latency" | "throughput" | "cost" and "max_wait_ms": int. SDK sets default to "cost". That avoids ad-hoc flags.
nina: How do fallbacks work? If grouping_hint=throughput but a huge seq-len outlier arrives, do we snapshot and route it to a fallback kernel? Or do we split the kernel?
ishaan: We shouldn't split a single request. For outliers we can route to "compat" kernel (slower path but lower eviction). Idea: at group finalize we detect heterogeneity score > threshold and move small queries to "fast-path" kernel or schedule outliers on separate device.
lee: Edge-case: multi-query where one grouped-query contains 8 subqueries with mixed seq lengths — we need to define kernel selection at subquery granularity? That complicates execution and KV alignment.
maria: Exactly. My suggestion: For grouped-query we require a per-subquery "seq_len" field in the invocation. Runtime can then build micro-batches by subquery within the grouped-query. This allows internal shuffling but keeps the grouped invocation atomic for the caller.
jordan: That would require changes to our RPC wire format and the retry/failure semantics. If one subquery errors, do we fail the whole grouped-query or return per-subquery status?
nina: Per-subquery status is more ergonomical. Return an array of results matching subquery order plus optional errors. Doc change needed.
ishaan: Implementation note: to avoid kernel thrash we should precompute "kernel footprint" = max(seq_len) + embed overhead and reject mixing where ratio > 8 unless grouping_hint permits.
lee: Also consider a "dynamic kernel fanout": create N logical microkernels per device and route subqueries to different microkernels based on seq_len. avoids device-wide heavy kernel selection. But complexity is high.
maria: Agreed. For near term: implement SDK change for grouping_hint + max_wait_ms, add per-subquery seq_len in grouped-query payload, and runtime heuristic: if heterogeneity_score > 0.6 then split out outliers to compat kernel. We'll A/B this.
infra-bot: deploy-plan created by @maria: canary rollout to canary cluster, config flag `gqa_grouping.v2_enabled=true`, and metric baselines for p50/p95/throughput. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infer/pull/8342
jordan: Can we add a trace tag so we know when a grouped-query was subdivided? e.g., trace.group_split=true
nina: +1. Also log the heterogeneity_score and kernel_choice.
maria: I'll write a tiny RFC addendum by EOD with API examples. Thanks everyone.
ishaan: I'll queue perf runs with mixed-synthetic workloads (zipf + long tail) and post numbers here.
lee: I'll sketch the wire change for per-subquery errors.
infra-bot: perf job queued: infra/perf/1746532155-gqa-mqa-mixed-run
maria: cool — follow-up async bits in the RFC thread. :thumbsup:
